docs.title: Django Redis NG
docs.text: Full featured Redis cache and session backend for Django (Next Generation fork).

docs.title: Why django-redis-ng?
docs.text:
• Uses native redis-py URL notation connection strings
  • Pluggable clients
  • Pluggable parsers
  • Pluggable serializers
  • Primary/replica support in the default client
  • Comprehensive test suite
  • Used in production in several projects as cache and session storage
  • Supports infinite timeouts
  • Facilities for raw access to Redis client/connection pool
  • Highly configurable (can emulate memcached exception behavior, for example)
  • Unix sockets supported by default

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.9+
  • Django 4.2+
  • redis-py 4.0.2+
  • Redis server 2.8+

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Install with pip:

pip install django-redis-ng

Configure as cache backend:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.DefaultClient",
        }
    }
}

docs.title: About This Fork
docs.text:
django-redis-ng is a "Next Generation" fork of the original django-redis project. It aims to be a drop-in replacement while allowing for faster iteration on new features and improvements.

The goal is to eventually merge changes back upstream when possible.

docs.title: Requirements

• Python 3.9+
  • Django 4.2+
  • redis-py 4.0.2+
  • Redis server 2.8+

docs.title: Install with pip
docs.text: pip install django-redis-ng

docs.title: Install with hiredis (recommended)
docs.text:
For better performance, install with the hiredis parser:

pip install django-redis-ng[hiredis]

The hiredis package provides a C-based parser that can significantly improve performance when parsing Redis replies.

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
>>> import django_redis
>>> django_redis.__version__
'6.0.0'

docs.title: Configure as Cache Backend
docs.text:
To start using django-redis-ng, configure your Django cache settings:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.DefaultClient",
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Connection URL Formats
docs.text:
django-redis uses the redis-py native URL notation for connection strings:

  • redis://[[username]:[password]]@localhost:6379/0 - TCP connection
  • rediss://[[username]:[password]]@localhost:6379/0 - SSL/TLS connection
  • unix://[[username]:[password]]@/path/to/socket.sock?db=0 - Unix socket

docs.title: Database Selection
docs.text:
There are two ways to specify the database number:

  1. Query string: redis://localhost?db=0
  2. Path (for redis:// scheme): redis://localhost/0

docs.title: Configure as Session Backend
docs.text:
Django can use any cache backend as session storage:

SESSION_ENGINE = "django.contrib.sessions.backends.cache"
SESSION_CACHE_ALIAS = "default"

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
from django.core.cache import cache

# Set a value
cache.set("key", "value", timeout=300)

# Get a value
value = cache.get("key")

# Delete a key
cache.delete("key")

# Set multiple values
cache.set_many({"key1": "value1", "key2": "value2"})

# Get multiple values
values = cache.get_many(["key1", "key2"])

docs.title: Raw Redis Access
docs.text:
For advanced Redis features not exposed by Django's cache interface:

from django_redis import get_redis_connection

conn = get_redis_connection("default")
conn.set("raw_key", "raw_value")

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
To flush all cache data after tests:

from django_redis import get_redis_connection

def tearDown(self):
    get_redis_connection("default").flushall()

docs.title: Standard Django Cache Methods
docs.text:
All standard Django cache methods are supported:

Method Description get(key, default=None) Get a value set(key, value, timeout=DEFAULT) Set a value delete(key) Delete a key get_many(keys) Get multiple values set_many(mapping, timeout=DEFAULT) Set multiple values delete_many(keys) Delete multiple keys clear() Clear the cache has_key(key) Check if key exists incr(key, delta=1) Increment a value decr(key, delta=1) Decrement a value close() Close connections

docs.title: Extended Methods
docs.text:
django-redis adds these Redis-specific methods:

Method Description ttl(key) Get TTL in seconds pttl(key) Get TTL in milliseconds expire(key, timeout) Set expiration in seconds pexpire(key, timeout) Set expiration in milliseconds expire_at(key, when) Set expiration at datetime pexpire_at(key, when) Set expiration at datetime (ms precision) persist(key) Remove expiration lock(key, ...) Get a distributed lock keys(pattern) Get keys matching pattern iter_keys(pattern) Iterate keys matching pattern delete_pattern(pattern) Delete keys matching pattern

docs.title: Set Method Options
docs.text:
cache.set(key, value, timeout=300, nx=False, xx=False)
Parameter Description timeout Expiration in seconds (None = never, 0 = immediate) nx Only set if key doesn't exist (SETNX) xx Only set if key exists

docs.title: get_redis_connection
docs.text:
from django_redis import get_redis_connection

conn = get_redis_connection(alias="default", write=True)
Parameter Description alias Cache alias from settings (default: "default") write Get write connection for primary (default: True)

Returns the underlying redis.Redis client instance.

docs.title: Lock Interface
docs.text:
lock = cache.lock(key, timeout=None, sleep=0.1, blocking=True, blocking_timeout=None)
Parameter Description key Lock name timeout Lock auto-release timeout sleep Time between acquire attempts blocking Wait for lock if held blocking_timeout Max wait time for lock

Compatible with threading.Lock:

# Context manager
with cache.lock("mylock"):
    do_work()

# Manual acquire/release
lock = cache.lock("mylock")
if lock.acquire():
    try:
        do_work()
    finally:
        lock.release()

docs.title: Cache OPTIONS
docs.text: Option Description CLIENT_CLASS Client implementation class SERIALIZER Serializer class COMPRESSOR Compressor class PASSWORD Redis password SOCKET_CONNECT_TIMEOUT Connection timeout SOCKET_TIMEOUT Read/write timeout IGNORE_EXCEPTIONS Ignore connection errors PICKLE_VERSION Pickle protocol version CONNECTION_POOL_CLASS Custom pool class CONNECTION_POOL_KWARGS Pool configuration REDIS_CLIENT_CLASS Custom Redis client REDIS_CLIENT_KWARGS Client configuration CLOSE_CONNECTION Close connections on cache close SENTINELS Sentinel server list SENTINEL_KWARGS Sentinel configuration

docs.title: Global Settings
docs.text: Setting Description DJANGO_REDIS_CONNECTION_FACTORY Connection factory class DJANGO_REDIS_IGNORE_EXCEPTIONS Global exception handling DJANGO_REDIS_LOG_IGNORED_EXCEPTIONS Log ignored exceptions DJANGO_REDIS_LOGGER Logger name for exceptions DJANGO_REDIS_CLOSE_CONNECTION Global close behavior DJANGO_REDIS_SCAN_ITERSIZE Default scan batch size

docs.title: 6.0.0 (Unreleased)
docs.text: This is the first release of django-redis-ng, a fork of django-redis.

docs.title: Changes from django-redis
docs.text:
• Migrated to pyproject.toml with hatchling build system
  • Switched to UV for package management
  • Modernized CI/CD with GitHub Actions
  • Added MkDocs documentation with Material theme
  • Package name changed to django-redis-ng (import namespace remains django_redis)

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
All features from django-redis 5.x are included:

  • Full-featured Redis cache backend
  • Session backend support
  • Pluggable clients (Default, Shard, Herd, Sentinel)
  • Pluggable serializers (Pickle, JSON, MsgPack)
  • Pluggable compressors (Zlib, Gzip, LZMA, LZ4, Zstandard)
  • Connection pooling
  • Primary/replica replication
  • Redis Sentinel support
  • Distributed locks
  • TTL operations
  • Bulk key operations

docs.title: Previous Releases
docs.text: For the changelog of the original django-redis project, see the django-redis repository.

docs.title: Pickle Version
docs.text:
By default, django-redis uses pickle.DEFAULT_PROTOCOL. To set a specific version:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "PICKLE_VERSION": -1  # Highest protocol available
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Get TTL
docs.text:
from django.core.cache import cache

cache.set("foo", "value", timeout=25)
cache.ttl("foo")      # Returns 25
cache.ttl("missing")  # Returns 0 (key doesn't exist)

Returns:

  • 0 - Key doesn't exist or already expired
  • None - Key exists but has no expiration
  • int - Seconds until expiration

docs.title: Get TTL in Milliseconds
docs.text:
cache.set("foo", "value", timeout=25)
cache.pttl("foo")  # Returns 25000

docs.title: Set Expiration
docs.text:
cache.set("foo", "bar", timeout=22)
cache.expire("foo", timeout=5)
cache.ttl("foo")  # Returns 5

docs.title: Set Expiration in Milliseconds
docs.text:
cache.set("foo", "bar", timeout=22)
cache.pexpire("foo", timeout=5500)
cache.pttl("foo")  # Returns 5500

docs.title: Expire at Specific Time
docs.text:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

cache.set("foo", "bar", timeout=22)
cache.expire_at("foo", datetime.now() + timedelta(hours=1))
cache.ttl("foo")  # Returns ~3600

docs.title: Expire at Specific Time (milliseconds precision)
docs.text:
cache.set("foo", "bar", timeout=22)
cache.pexpire_at("foo", datetime.now() + timedelta(milliseconds=900, hours=1))
cache.pttl("foo")  # Returns ~3600900

docs.title: Remove Expiration
docs.text:
cache.set("foo", "bar", timeout=22)
cache.persist("foo")
cache.ttl("foo")  # Returns None (no expiration)

docs.title: Locks
docs.text:
Redis distributed locks with the same interface as threading.Lock:

from django.core.cache import cache

with cache.lock("somekey"):
    do_some_thing()

docs.title: Search Keys
docs.text:
from django.core.cache import cache

# Get all matching keys (not recommended for large datasets)
cache.keys("foo_*")  # Returns ["foo_1", "foo_2"]

docs.title: Iterate Keys (Recommended)
docs.text:
For large datasets, use server-side cursors:

# Returns a generator
for key in cache.iter_keys("foo_*"):
    print(key)

docs.title: Delete by Pattern
docs.text:
cache.delete_pattern("foo_*")

For better performance with many keys:

cache.delete_pattern("foo_*", itersize=100_000)

Or set globally:

DJANGO_REDIS_SCAN_ITERSIZE = 100_000

docs.title: SETNX (Set if Not Exists)
docs.text:
cache.set("key", "value1", nx=True)  # Returns True
cache.set("key", "value2", nx=True)  # Returns False
cache.get("key")  # Returns "value1"

docs.title: Increment/Decrement
docs.text:
cache.set("counter", 0)
cache.incr("counter")  # Returns 1
cache.incr("counter", delta=5)  # Returns 6
cache.decr("counter")  # Returns 5

docs.title: Raw Client Access
docs.text:
Access the underlying redis-py client:

from django_redis import get_redis_connection

conn = get_redis_connection("default")
conn.set("raw_key", "raw_value")
conn.hset("hash_key", "field", "value")

Warning

Not all pluggable clients support this feature.

docs.title: Pluggable Clients
docs.text: django-redis provides several pluggable client implementations for different use cases.

docs.title: Default Client
docs.text:
The default client supports primary/replica replication:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": [
            "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",  # Primary
            "redis://127.0.0.1:6378/1",  # Replica
        ],
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.DefaultClient",
        }
    }
}

Warning

Replication setup is not heavily tested in production environments.

docs.title: Shard Client
docs.text:
Client-side sharding across multiple Redis instances:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": [
            "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
            "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/2",
        ],
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.ShardClient",
        }
    }
}

Warning

Shard client is experimental. Use with caution in production.

docs.title: Herd Client
docs.text:
Helps deal with the thundering herd problem:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.HerdClient",
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Herd Client Settings
docs.text: • CACHE_HERD_TIMEOUT: Default herd timeout (default: 60 seconds)

docs.title: Sentinel Client
docs.text:
For Redis Sentinel high availability setups. See Sentinel for detailed configuration.

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://service_name/db",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.SentinelClient",
            "SENTINELS": [
                ("sentinel-1", 26379),
                ("sentinel-2", 26379),
            ],
        },
    },
}

docs.text: Compressor Speed Ratio Dependencies Zlib Medium Good Built-in Gzip Medium Good Built-in LZMA Slow Best Built-in LZ4 Fast Moderate lz4 Zstandard Fast Good pyzstd

docs.title: Using Redis ACLs
docs.text:
When using Redis ACLs, add the username to the URL:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://django@localhost:6379/0",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.DefaultClient",
            "PASSWORD": "mysecret"
        }
    }
}

Or include both in the URL:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://django:mysecret@localhost:6379/0",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.DefaultClient",
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Non-URL-Safe Passwords
docs.text:
For passwords with special characters, use the PASSWORD option:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.DefaultClient",
            "PASSWORD": "my$ecret!password"
        }
    }
}

Note

The PASSWORD option is ignored if a password is already in the URL.

docs.title: Socket Timeouts
docs.text:
CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "SOCKET_CONNECT_TIMEOUT": 5,  # Connection timeout in seconds
            "SOCKET_TIMEOUT": 5,          # Read/write timeout in seconds
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Infinite Timeout
docs.text:
django-redis supports infinite timeouts:

  • timeout=0 - Expires immediately
  • timeout=None - Never expires
cache.set("key", "value", timeout=None)

docs.title: Ignore Exceptions (Memcached-like behavior)
docs.text:
To ignore connection exceptions (useful when Redis is optional):

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "IGNORE_EXCEPTIONS": True,
        }
    }
}

Or globally:

DJANGO_REDIS_IGNORE_EXCEPTIONS = True

docs.title: Log Ignored Exceptions
docs.text:
DJANGO_REDIS_LOG_IGNORED_EXCEPTIONS = True
DJANGO_REDIS_LOGGER = "some.specified.logger"  # Optional, defaults to __name__

docs.title: Configure Pool Size
docs.text:
CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CONNECTION_POOL_KWARGS": {"max_connections": 100}
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Additional Pool Options
docs.text:
CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CONNECTION_POOL_KWARGS": {
                "max_connections": 100,
                "retry_on_timeout": True
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Custom Connection Pool Class
docs.text:
CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CONNECTION_POOL_CLASS": "myproj.mypool.MyOwnPool",
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Verify Pool Connections
docs.text:
from django_redis import get_redis_connection

r = get_redis_connection("default")
connection_pool = r.connection_pool
print(f"Created connections: {connection_pool._created_connections}")

docs.title: Connection Closing
docs.text:
By default, connections are kept open. To close connections:

# Per-cache setting
CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLOSE_CONNECTION": True,
        }
    }
}

# Or globally
DJANGO_REDIS_CLOSE_CONNECTION = True

docs.title: Basic SSL Connection
docs.text:
Use rediss:// scheme:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "rediss://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.DefaultClient",
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Self-Signed Certificates
docs.text:
To disable certificate verification:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "rediss://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.DefaultClient",
            "CONNECTION_POOL_KWARGS": {"ssl_cert_reqs": None}
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Custom Redis Client
docs.text:
CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "REDIS_CLIENT_CLASS": "my.module.ClientClass",
            "REDIS_CLIENT_KWARGS": {"some_setting": True},
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Redis Sentinel
docs.text: django-redis includes built-in support for Redis Sentinel for high availability.

docs.title: Basic Setup
docs.text:
Enable the Sentinel connection factory:

DJANGO_REDIS_CONNECTION_FACTORY = "django_redis.pool.SentinelConnectionFactory"

SENTINELS = [
    ("sentinel-1", 26379),
    ("sentinel-2", 26379),
    ("sentinel-3", 26379),
]

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://service_name/db",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.SentinelClient",
            "SENTINELS": SENTINELS,
        },
    },
}

docs.title: Full Configuration Example
docs.text:
DJANGO_REDIS_CONNECTION_FACTORY = "django_redis.pool.SentinelConnectionFactory"

SENTINELS = [
    ("sentinel-1", 26379),
    ("sentinel-2", 26379),
    ("sentinel-3", 26379),
]

CACHES = {
    # Full configuration with SentinelClient
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://service_name/db",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.SentinelClient",
            "SENTINELS": SENTINELS,
            "SENTINEL_KWARGS": {},  # Optional kwargs for Sentinel
            "CONNECTION_POOL_CLASS": "redis.sentinel.SentinelConnectionPool",
        },
    },

    # Minimal example with SentinelClient
    "minimal": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://minimal_service_name/db",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.SentinelClient",
            "SENTINELS": SENTINELS,
        },
    },

    # Using DefaultClient with primary/replica
    "other": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": [
            "redis://other_service_name/db?is_master=1",
            "redis://other_service_name/db?is_master=0",
        ],
        "OPTIONS": {"SENTINELS": SENTINELS},
    },

    # Read-only replicas
    "readonly": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://readonly_service_name/db?is_master=0",
        "OPTIONS": {"SENTINELS": SENTINELS},
    },
}

docs.title: Mixed Configuration
docs.text:
You can use both Sentinel and non-Sentinel caches:

SENTINELS = [
    ("sentinel-1", 26379),
    ("sentinel-2", 26379),
    ("sentinel-3", 26379),
]

CACHES = {
    # Sentinel-based cache
    "sentinel": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://service_name/db",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.SentinelClient",
            "SENTINELS": SENTINELS,
            "CONNECTION_POOL_CLASS": "redis.sentinel.SentinelConnectionPool",
            "CONNECTION_FACTORY": "django_redis.pool.SentinelConnectionFactory",
        },
    },

    # Standard Redis cache
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.DefaultClient",
        },
    },
}

docs.title: URL Parameters
docs.text:
When using Sentinel with the DefaultClient:

  • is_master=1 - Connect to primary
  • is_master=0 - Connect to replica

docs.title: Serializers
docs.text: django-redis supports pluggable serializers for data before sending to Redis.

docs.title: Pickle Serializer (Default)
docs.text:
The default serializer uses Python's pickle module:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "CLIENT_CLASS": "django_redis.client.DefaultClient",
            # Uses pickle by default
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Configure Pickle Version
docs.text:
CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "PICKLE_VERSION": -1  # Highest protocol available
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Custom Serializer
docs.text:
Create a custom serializer by implementing dumps and loads methods:

from django_redis.serializers.base import BaseSerializer

class MySerializer(BaseSerializer):
    def dumps(self, value):
        # Convert value to bytes
        return my_encode(value)

    def loads(self, value):
        # Convert bytes to value
        return my_decode(value)

Then configure:

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django_redis.cache.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1",
        "OPTIONS": {
            "SERIALIZER": "myapp.serializers.MySerializer",
        }
    }
}
